title: Bind a value from Python
summary: An application should pass a value separately from SQL text.
introduction: An application should pass a value separately from SQL text. Your task: Insert a title containing an apostrophe through the bound value.
learningObjectives: Insert a title containing an apostrophe through the bound value.
Explain the example for bind a value from python

blocks.text: An application should pass a value separately from SQL text. Python's SQLite driver binds a value where the question-mark placeholder appears.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.code:
import sqlite3
with sqlite3.connect(":memory:") as connection:
    connection.execute("CREATE TABLE books(title TEXT)")
    connection.execute("INSERT INTO books VALUES (?)", ("Moon Trip",))
    print(connection.execute("SELECT title FROM books").fetchone()[0])
blocks.title: Bind a value from Python

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Run with Python 3 to print Moon Trip from a temporary in-memory database.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep the comma in the one-item tuple. Never join untrusted text into a SQL command instead of binding it.
